recipes.name: Simple Strawberry Sauce
ingredients_raw: 2 quarts fresh strawberries, cleaned, hulled and sliced

steps.text: Place strawberries in a large bowl. Sprinkle sugar evenly over berries; stir to coat. Let stand at room temperature, stirring occasionally, for 10 minutes.
Cover and chill in the refrigerator until ready to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Simple Strawberry Sauce
raw_recipe.description: Freshly sliced strawberries with sugar make a chunky, sweet sauce that requires no cooking. Delicious served with cheesecake, angel food cake, or pancakes.

review.reviewBody: Simple and delicious strawberry sauce. I cut this back to six servings. I threw this together to spoon over buttermilk pancakes. This is EXACTLY the same strawberry topping my Grandma always made to go over ice cream.

I disagree with the poster that said that this recipe should not need to be written. Perhaps for the people in the "older" generation that were able to watch their at-home-mothers cook every single day - she is right - but now things are different and rarely is home ec. even offered in schools anymore. The only thing I do differently is to add at least 1 1/2 cup water and some vanilla extract...and also some honey as well as sugar (to taste). I let sit overnight - we like the large amount of liquid - because I serve the strawberries over pound cake and the poud cake is just so much better with all that liquid soaked into it!!!

you can also make a sauce to pour over cheesecake by putting the strawberries in a blender and add powdered sugar instead of white sugar and pulse a few times, depending on how chuncky you want the strawberries.....

I make this except I use a potato masher to squash the juice out of the strawberries. Sometime I add about 1/4 cup water if the berries are not juicy ripe. We like ours with lots of juice to soak up the cake. Great over ice cream too.

As kids we used to go out with Mom to pick strawberries, then come home to make some batches to share, some to freeze and some for the week with shortcake. We used the classic Bisquick shortcakes and when we cleaned the berries we cut them in chunks. Mom never measured anything but was always in favor of starting with less and adding more later. We used “some” white sugar, mashed the berries a bit with a potato masher to help them give up their juice, and added “a little” warm water. By dinner time they were usually perfect for shortcake. I’m 67 now and have done it the same way for years. Sometimes I use sugar substitute if a guest needs me to but I think regular sugar brings the juices out best.
Thanks for posting this. Not everyone had their Mom. My Mom didn’t.

I wouldn't exactly call this a "sauce", however this is my favorite strawberry topping from way back in the day. (if you'd like more 
 of a sauce, give it a couple whirls in the blender or processor) My mom and grandma made this all the time. It's not really a "recipe" per se, but nonetheless, it's perfect on pound cake or angel food cake, topped with whipped cream. Try it with brown sugar for a nice change of pace! Yum!

My mother made this when I was a child, and I've been making this for 50 years. 10 minutes is not long enough. I let them sit until there is LOTS of sauce. The strawberries get pretty mushy. My mother would sometimes add a little sour cream and mix it in after all the juice was there, and it tastes like melted strawberry ice cream. YUM!

This is just how my mom used to make strawberry topping for strawberry shortcake. This needs to be made up in advance to eating though because after it stands a while the strawberries get softer and sweeter and the juice gets really syrupy. I used superfine sugar for this.
Very nice not so heavy desert when we ts hot. I added Bacardi rum to mine. That makes it so nice.

My market had a great sale on strawberries but since they are not in season, they weren’t very sweet. I used a little less sugar than this recipe called for and it made the strawberries taste like they were freshly picked.

I've been making this for a long time, but I wanted to see if there were alternatives that I may be missing. Nope....this is it! Simple, delicious and the nice syrup forms. I do rinse off the strawberries briefly with water, so that may help forming the syrup. In the past, I didn't let it sit out for 10 min, so that's good to know. I like to have with angel food cake, but all of the other ideas (ice cream, pancakes, etc) sound great!!
I made it as a frosting with my pound cake and enjoyed it very much.
Thank you for your help. Much appreciated.
I have done this for many years, mom taught me this back when I was a kid and her Mother taught her! So we've done this for over 100 years
Shouldn't you use a little lemon juice to spruce up the strawberries?
My 8yr. old grandson Max did all the work except slicing the strawberries. He says it was easy and delicious. We served over Mom's buttermilk pancakes. Another delicious recipe in Allrecipes!

My mom just passed away 2 weeks ago today. She used to make this to put on those lil strawberry shortcake bunts u find around the 🍓 when they r in season. I didn't get to get her to write down any of my grandma's recipes before she passed away but hopefully I can Google them and find some.
